rows.description: Each side tells friends a simple story in which the other is the villain. With time, memories of tenderness fade and the complicated person on the other side becomes a symbol.
graph_context: previous stage: The rupture
next stage: The parent's silent grief

rows.description: The father tells himself that the son is ungrateful, yet keeps his old room ready and reads his social posts in secret. Pride and hurt make it hard for him to reach out, and he may confuse waiting with dignity.
graph_context: previous stage: Distance and story-hardening
next stage: A go-between opens a door
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: gratitude, grief, confusion, pride

rows.subtype: Stage 5: A go-between opens a door [Observer]
rows.description: An aunt tells each that the other misses them, without pushing either. A neutral relative can carry a message of softness when direct contact is too risky for the pride of both.
graph_context: previous stage: The parent's silent grief
next stage: A small first meeting
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: pride

rows.description: They meet for tea, agree not to relitigate the past on day one and each says one true thing. Reunion works in small steps, and it may bring closeness without total agreement.
graph_context: previous stage: A go-between opens a door
this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26

rows.subtype: Stage 1: Values clash after marriage or career [Actor]
rows.description: A woman who married outside her community faces her parents' refusal to attend the wedding. She feels torn between love for her family and her right to choose her life, and the hurt on both sides is deep.
graph_context: next stage: Cutting contact to protect herself
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: affection, hurt

rows.subtype: Stage 2: Cutting contact to protect herself [Actor]
rows.description: Repeated painful calls lead her to stop answering. It may be a needed break from criticism, but as time passes it also becomes a habit that is hard to undo.
graph_context: previous stage: Values clash after marriage or career
next stage: Life events widen the gap
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.subtype: Stage 3: Life events widen the gap [Observer]
rows.description: A festival, a grandparent's illness or the birth of a child passes without the family together. Each milestone reopens the loss, and relatives urge her either to give in or to hold on.
graph_context: previous stage: Cutting contact to protect herself
next stage: The softening
this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22

rows.description: Her mother, after a health scare, realises how much time has been lost and dislikes being the parent who lost a child over a wedding. Fear of regret can loosen rigid positions on both sides.
graph_context: previous stage: Life events widen the gap
next stage: Terms for reunion

related mind states: fear, regret

rows.description: The daughter says "I would like to see you, and I will not accept insults about my husband." Setting conditions for contact protects the relationship rather than ending it, and where a relationship has been unsafe or abusive, distance can remain right.
graph_context: previous stage: The softening
next stage: An imperfect, honest reunion

rows.description: They rebuild slowly with short visits and learn to leave some topics unresolved. Warmth returns in ordinary acts such as a shared meal, and hurt is acknowledged rather than erased.
